NASA's Swift space telescope is expected to crash back to Earth in the next few days. The Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory will reenter Earth's atmosphere in an uncontrolled fashion, after a robotic rescue mission failed to boost the scope to a higher orbit. Swift launched to Earth orbit back in November 2004. Over the next two decades, it studied gamma-ray bursts — the most powerful explosions in the universe — and other cosmic objects and events using a trio of telescopes: a Burst Alert Telescope (BAT), an X-Ray Telescope (XRT), and its Ultraviolet/Optical Telescope (UVOT). On Oct. 20, NASA reported that Swift's orbit had decayed to 171 miles (275 kilometers) above Earth and that the roughly 3,300-pound (1,500-kilogram) observatory was no longer able to compensate for the effects of the increased drag. It entered safe mode, followed by Swift's operations team at Pennsylvania State University sending a command to the spacecraft that effectively ended its operations ahead of its destructive and fiery nose-dive. It's unclear at the moment exactly when and where Swift will plunge to Earth. But researchers definitely have their eyes peeled. In physics fashion, for the most part, what goes up must come down — with more space hardware to follow. Thanks to the growing surge in low Earth orbit constellations and technology refresh cycles, there are 10 times more objects reentering per year than there were just five years ago, said Darren McKnight, a senior technical fellow at LeoLabs, a company that keeps a watchful eye on what's going on above our planet. "It is unfortunate that Swift was not 'reorbited,' but from a reentry hazard perspective it is a small portion of the stuff coming back in. The rub on this, of course, is that, while many people bemoan the reentry of more objects , I am much more upset about the rapid rate of abandoning massive objects above 400 miles [644 km]," McKnight told Space.com. Swift will likely disintegrate sufficiently upon reentry to not pose a ground casualty hazard, McKnight said. Wednesday’s disaster – one of Europe’s deadliest rail accidents this century – has seen victims’ relatives endure an agonising wait as forensics teams identify the dead, sometimes from individual body parts. A legal body set up to handle the identification work, made up of police and forensics experts, announced in a statement late on Sunday the 10 latest confirmed foreign victims. It had already announced the deaths of a French and a Portuguese citizen, as well as that of 54 Spaniards. All but three of the victims are now identified, the statement added. Three reports for missing people remain active, the authorities said. They concern two Australians and one Japanese citizen. “As the contacted families have expressed their wish to travel to Spain to carry out in-person identification, we are awaiting their arrival in the country,” the statement said. The accident was Spain’s second high-speed train collision this year and raised fresh questions about the country’s rail safety, after a crash in the southern region of Andalusia in January killed 46 people. The latest disaster struck when a service by state operator Renfe ploughed into the back of a stationary train belonging to Spanish company Iryo outside the central village of Urda, around 130km (80 miles) south of Madrid. The failure of an automatic safety system halted all trains on a 63km stretch of track, but a control centre authorised the Renfe service to resume its journey while the other train was still. clusters.title: Paddy procurement to begin in Prayagraj region on Nov 2 | Hindustan Times
clusters.text: Paddy procurement in the Prayagraj division is set to begin on November 2, with the administration targeting the purchase of 5.63 lakh metric tonnes (MT) of the crop across its four districts.In a first, officials have introduced QR codes for rice bags on a pilot basis to facilitate digital tracking and curb black marketing. Furthermore, officials confirmed that all paddy transportation will be conducted exclusively via GPS-enabled trucks.The procurement drive for the 2026-27 kharif marketing season, originally scheduled for November 1 in eastern Uttar Pradesh, was deferred by one day due to a holiday. The process will continue through February 28, 2027.Another significant update this season is the accelerated payment schedule for farmers. Payments, which previously took three to four days, will now be credited directly to farmers’ bank accounts within 48 hours of verification via the Public Financial Management System (PFMS).“Several steps have been taken to streamline the procurement process for farmers. Those who have completed their Farmer Registry can now have their paddy weighed directly, bypassing the need for a separate online registration process,” said Raju Patel, divisional food marketing controller, Prayagraj.The division has approved 361 procurement centres: 159 in Prayagraj, 96 in Pratapgarh, 65 in Fatehpur, and 41 in Kaushambi. Prayagraj leads with a procurement target of 2.80 lakh MT, followed by Fatehpur (1.15 lakh MT), Pratapgarh (1.06 lakh MT), and Kaushambi (62,000 MT).According to Patel, 4,513 farmers have registered for the procurement process thus far: 1,632 from Prayagraj, 1,599 from Fatehpur, 946 from Kaushambi, and 336 from Pratapgarh.The minimum support price (MSP) for the season has also been announced, with common variety paddy set at ₹2,441 per quintal and Grade A paddy at ₹2,461 per quintal.

clusters.text: Prayagraj: Anticipating a surge in passenger traffic during Diwali and Chhath, the Uttar Pradesh State Road Transport Corporation (UPSRTC) will operate 148 additional bus trips daily from the Prayagraj region between Nov 6 and 17.The extra services will run on seven major routes, with the highest number of trips planned for Varanasi, Lucknow and Gorakhpur. The corporation has designed the schedule to ensure buses are available at intervals ranging from five to 20 minutes, depending on the route.On the Prayagraj-Lucknow route, 34 additional trips will be operated, with a bus available every 10 minutes. The Prayagraj-Ayodhya route will have 20 extra trips at 15-minute intervals, while 24 additional trips will run on the Prayagraj-Kanpur route every 20 minutes.The Prayagraj-Varanasi route will see the highest frequency, with 24 additional trips and buses available every five minutes. On the Prayagraj-Jaunpur-Gorakhpur route, 26 extra trips will be operated at 15-minute intervals. The Prayagraj-Mirzapur and Prayagraj-Banda routes will have 10 additional trips each, with buses available every 20 minutes and 15 minutes, respectively.UPSRTC has also announced an incentive scheme for drivers, conductors and workshop staff engaged in operating the additional services during the festive period.Meanwhile, Railways has also planned special trains to handle the festival rush. The Anand Vihar Terminal-Chhapra special will run from Nov 3 to 17.
